- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model consistently under-responds to recent price spikes; if last 3–5 days show sharp upward movement, add 0.5–1.5x the spike magnitude to forecast.
- Model over-anticipates mean reversion; if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, avoid forcing downward correction unless price is >10% above 30-day moving average.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing sentiment-driven momentum; apply a 1–3 day lag correction for sentiment-driven price acceleration.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to overfit recent trend; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day moving average) to sentiment before weighting forecast adjustments.
